person.name: Praneeth Papishetty
person.headline: Storage engineer. Relational and NoSQL data systems.
person.tagline: I build data systems and the tools that keep them running.
summary: I have worked with databases for 13 years.
I started as an Oracle DBA. Then I ran Cassandra, ScyllaDB, Couchbase and MySQL NDB at AT&T.
At Warner Bros. Discovery, I built the platform that deployed databases for HBO Max.
Now I work on Vitess and MySQL at Slack.

lines: I move Slack's vttablets to Shipyard, the new EC2 platform.
I build tools that run vttablets in containers. This makes configuration management easier.
I write tooling in Go and Python.

link.label: About Shipyard, on the Slack engineering blog

windows.note: Joined HBO through Metis Software Solutions in 2019. Full time at WBD from 2021.
lines: I built DIM, a self-service platform for database deployments. Provisioning time went from 3 weeks to 12 hours. Support requests went down by about 50%. Three other teams now use the same pattern.
I co-designed the RDS major-version upgrade pipeline with DMS and CDC. Downtime was near zero. Manual work went down by about 80%.
I wrote composite Terraform modules and a Checkov auto-review. Deployment time for EMEA and APAC went down by about 70%.
I built a database connection tool with Homebrew, Docker and Steampipe. Support volume went down by about 30%.
I redesigned an architecture and cut its AWS cost by about 80%.
I automated Cassandra rebuilds and multi-datacenter scaling. Manual work went down by about 60%.
I built a dashboard for HBO Max client metrics, for an internal project.

I fixed unpredictable compaction on DataStax Cassandra. TTLs ranged from seconds to days. The app team moved to predictable TTLs. I moved the tables to time-window compaction. Compaction time, CPU load and I/O load went down.
I tuned and automated Cassandra repairs with Prometheus and Grafana. Repair time went down by about 80%.
I put Oracle GoldenGate replication into production: one-way, two-way and cascade, with Veridata checks.
I ran ScyllaDB, Couchbase, MariaDB and MySQL NDB clusters in production.
I planned capacity for each iPhone launch, three months ahead.
I ran more than 30 Oracle instances. One production database was 14 TB.
I tuned SQL and indexes with AWR, ADDM and TKPROF. Peak-hour latency on bookings went down by about 50%.
I archived old reservations from Oracle to MSSQL with SSIS.
I led the schedule for an offshore team of four DBAs.
